a.problem: touching_merges always returns False, so intervals sharing an endpoint that at least one of them contains (e.g. [0,1] and [1,2]) are never merged, making normalize/union/intersection/difference return non-canonical, fragmented output.

b.problem: The change to the core merge rule removes the docstring stating the touching invariant and adds no regression tests, so the behaviour change went undetected (the repo has no tests at all).
